back: Local: one model per series. Global: one model trained on many series. Global handles short and new series better and is easier to serve.
Series count × time per series ÷ number of cores. Add fixed costs for reading and writing data.
A new item with little or no history. Global models or group averages can give a first forecast.
Partition by series id, batch many series per task, keep series together, and score only changed series.

front: What belongs in a fallback chain?
back: Primary model, then a simple model such as seasonal naive, then the last known forecast. Log which level was used.
Cost grows silently with catalogue size. Cost per run shows if a model change is worth its compute.
